attacks.claim: The 'never interrupted' freeze/heat protection claim is contradicted by the design. Relays are held open for the ~90 s install, and the 7 °C / 32 °C guard is checked only before install starts, not during it. Power loss or a failed verify mid-install leaves heating or cooling off with no stated recovery time, and the 32 °C branch has no test result.
attacks.evidence: "During the ~90 s install, relays are held open (off). Install is deferred if indoor temperature is below 7 °C or above 32 °C, so freeze/heat protection is never interrupted." QA shows only "Temperature deferral at 5 °C chamber test | Pass".

attacks.claim: Power-stealing installs are excluded from the HIL matrix, yet they are part of the fleet. Holding relays open for 90 s on a power-stealing thermostat could brown out or reset the unit mid-install, and no test shows this is safe.
attacks.evidence: "HIL bench: conventional 1H/1C, 2-stage, heat pump + aux, no C-wire power stealing; rev B/C/D | Pass, 0 relay faults over 72 h"

attacks.claim: Automatic revert triggers only on boot failure or failed post-boot self-test. A 4.8 build that boots and passes self-test but hangs, drops Wi-Fi, or misdrives relays has no automatic revert. Recovery depends on the 0.1%/6 h page threshold, human action, and a multi-day cloud push, with no stated time-to-mitigate.
attacks.evidence: "If 4.8 fails to boot or fails its post-boot self-test 3 times, the unit reverts to 4.7 automatically."

attacks.claim: Halt and revert both depend on the same OTA service and CDN. If that path fails, units cannot be halted or reverted, and no fallback channel is named. This conflicts with the agreed requirement that devices must always be able to return to the previous firmware.
attacks.evidence: "Halt: pause the OTA campaign (one switch)" and "Revert: push 4.7 to updated units through the same OTA path"

attacks.claim: The revert path is asserted to work, but the only evidence is that it was 'tested on 300 qa-fleet units' with no pass/fail result, failure count, or rollback row in the QA table. Revert behavior at 612k units under halt-and-revert load is unverified, and the test scale is far below fleet size.
attacks.evidence: "Revert: push 4.7 to updated units through the same OTA path; ... Tested on 300 `qa-fleet` units." ABSENT: revert pass/fail result or any rollback row in the QA summary.

attacks.claim: Editing a schedule on 4.7 discards the cloud's v2 copy, and the v1 copy keeps only 4 of up to 8 periods. A later re-upgrade cannot restore the user's original 8-period schedule, so user data is lost with no recovery path. The re-upgrade path is also untested.
attacks.evidence: "When a unit on 4.7 edits its schedule, the cloud discards the stale v2 copy, so a later re-upgrade starts from the current v1 schedule." QA covers only "edit on 4.8, downgrade to 4.7".

attacks.claim: The v2-to-v1 projection rule is underspecified. The artifact does not say how ties are broken, what happens when several periods map to one anchor, or what happens when an anchor has no nearby period. The 4.7 schedule after downgrade depends on this output, and the selection logic is not validated against a defined 'correct'.
attacks.evidence: "keeping the 4 periods closest to the user's wake / leave / return / sleep anchors"

attacks.claim: A 9.2-or-older app may edit a 4-period schedule on a 4.8 unit and write only v1, while the cloud still holds a v2 copy. The artifact does not say which copy 4.8 reads in that case, so a stale v2 could silently override the user's edit.
attacks.evidence: "App 9.2 and older can view but not edit 8-period schedules" and "When a unit on 4.7 edits its schedule, the cloud discards the stale v2 copy". ABSENT: how a 9.2 edit on a 4.8 unit's schedule is reconciled.

attacks.claim: Home/Away state is occupancy-derived personal data, but the artifact does not state the storage region or hosting location for it. For a US/Canada fleet with Canadian users, residency and cross-border handling are unspecified.
attacks.evidence: "Only the resulting Home/Away state is sent to the cloud ... it is kept 7 days and then deleted." ABSENT: storage region and hosting location.

attacks.claim: The 7-day deletion and turn-off deletion claims do not say whether Home/Away events are linked to an account or device ID, whether backups or logs are covered, or whether the telemetry copy (which the cost section says is ingested) is purged. The privacy promise covers only the app copy. The partner-API non-exposure claim has no isolation test in the QA table.
attacks.evidence: "it is kept 7 days and then deleted"; "Turning it off deletes stored Home/Away history."; "Home/Away state adds ~1 small event per state change; projected +0.4% on telemetry ingest."; "Home/Away state is not exposed through the partner integrations API." ABSENT: identifier scheme, deletion scope, telemetry retention, and partner-API verification.

attacks.claim: The campaign halt and the mass revert push are described without any statement of who can operate them, how operators authenticate, or whether a push needs approval. A compromised operator account could mass-push firmware to 612k units.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: authn/authz and approval for the OTA halt and revert controls. Text: "pause the OTA campaign (one switch)" and "push 4.7 to updated units through the same OTA path".

attacks.claim: Away Assist treats 2 h without motion as absence. A seated or sleeping occupant outside the sensor's view gets Away setpoints during a scheduled home period, and the artifact gives no false-Away rate, miss rate, recovery path, or test for stationary occupants. The feature is off by default, which limits exposure but does not remove the gap.
attacks.evidence: "the thermostat's built-in motion sensor sets Away mode after 2 h with no motion during scheduled 'home' periods"; ABSENT: false-Away rate, sensor miss rate, or stationary-occupant testing.

attacks.claim: The 6% median runtime claim is published with a 412-home trial and a linked methodology page, but the artifact does not show the results or confirm the page is live before the notes and listing go out.
attacks.evidence: "In our 2025-26 field trial of 412 homes, Away Assist cut heating runtime by a median of 6%." and "hearthline.com/away-assist-trial (reviewed by legal for substantiation, LGL-4472)"

attacks.claim: Install windows are synchronized at 02:00–05:00 local, so OTA downloads cluster in a few hours. Peak concurrency, retries, and resumes are not analyzed, and the 1.5 TB figure is a single-pass total, not a peak-load estimate.
attacks.evidence: "OTA egress: 2.4 MB image × 612k units ≈ 1.5 TB via existing CDN contract, within the monthly commit." and "Install window 02:00-05:00 local"

attacks.claim: Wi-Fi reconnect is faster but no jitter, backoff, or cloud connection-rate limit is stated. After a regional outage ends, many units could reconnect together and create a connection storm.
attacks.evidence: "Wi-Fi reconnect after router reboot now < 60 s." ABSENT: reconnect jitter, backoff, or rate limits.

attacks.claim: Away Assist emits a cloud event per state change, and transitions are tied to shared schedule boundaries and a 2 h timer. Correlated bursts and flapping near the threshold are not bounded, and the +0.4% telemetry projection assumes a steady rate.
attacks.evidence: "Home/Away state adds ~1 small event per state change; projected +0.4% on telemetry ingest."

attacks.claim: Stage gates use absolute thresholds, such as a boot-revert rate below 0.05% on ~6,100 units (about 3 units), with no sample-size or statistical basis. Those thresholds would behave differently at other fleet sizes.
attacks.evidence: "boot-revert rate < 0.05%" with "1% (~6,100) | 3 days"

attacks.claim: Monitoring has no alert on HVAC fault codes or schedule-sync errors. Those signals appear only on a dashboard, and the advance gate depends on HVAC fault telemetry. The paging threshold (boot reverts above 0.1%) is also looser than the 0.05% stage gate, so a regression can persist for a 4-day stage before anyone is paged.
attacks.evidence: "Fleet dashboard by version, rev and HVAC type: boot reverts, self-test failures, offline rate, HVAC fault codes, schedule-sync errors." and "Pages firmware on-call if boot reverts exceed 0.1%..."

attacks.claim: The QA table has no test for power loss, network loss, or OTA interruption mid-download or mid-install, and no test of a revert with an HVAC call active. Partial-failure coverage is thin for a fleet this size.
attacks.evidence: QA table lists only "Failed-boot injection → auto revert to 4.7 | Pass".

attacks.claim: Key custody and rotation for the Ed25519 image-signing key are not described. Compromise of that key would allow arbitrary signed firmware fleet-wide.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: signing key storage, access control, and rotation. Text: "Images are signed (Ed25519)".

attacks.claim: Anti-rollback is intentionally not incremented, so signed 4.7 stays installable. The artifact gives no plan for handling known 4.7 vulnerabilities across the fleet, and the anti-rollback counter readback is not shown in QA.
attacks.evidence: "4.8 does not increment the secure-boot anti-rollback counter (no security fixes in this release), so 4.7 remains installable." ABSENT: counter readback before and after install.

attacks.claim: Existing users start sending occupancy-derived state to the cloud after an OTA. Away Assist is off by default and the toggle explains what is stored, which mitigates this. The artifact does not show the consent text or how existing users are told about the privacy notice change.
attacks.evidence: "Privacy notice section 3 updated (legal review LGL-4471)." ABSENT: consent text and notice to existing users.

attacks.claim: The 4.8 change to Wi-Fi reconnect behavior on an RF device sold in the US and Canada is not shown to have been assessed for FCC or ISED permissive-change scope.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: RF certification assessment for 4.8.

attacks.claim: Schedule state is kept in two representations, one of which is a hand-maintained lossy projection, plus a cloud-side invalidation step. Away Assist also couples motion state, setpoints, schedules, and history retention. Neither has a stated contract test or isolation seam.
attacks.evidence: "keeping the 4 periods closest to the user's wake / leave / return / sleep anchors; the cloud stores both." and "the cloud discards the stale v2 copy"

attacks.claim: The artifact does not say which hardware revisions include the built-in motion sensor. Rollout is stratified across rev B, C and D, so Away Assist could be inert or behave differently on some boards.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: per-revision motion-sensor availability. "Hardware: rev B 22%, rev C 51%, rev D 27%".

attacks.claim: The stage 1 advance check uses only 3 days of data, and stage 4 has no duration. The rollout starts 10 Nov, so a heating-season fault could reach the full fleet before it appears. The public 'next two weeks' message does not match the plan, which has no end date at stage 4.
attacks.evidence: "| 1 | 1% (~6,100) | 3 days |" and "| 4 | 100% | — | — |" and "Rolling out over the next two weeks."

attacks.claim: The 'Some schedule changes were simplified' notice does not say which periods were dropped, so a user cannot tell whether the schedule is still correct. The French notice and the 9.2 update prompt are not shown to be localized or accessibility-tested.
attacks.evidence: "The app shows 'Some schedule changes were simplified' if v2 had more than 4 periods." and "App 9.2 viewing an 8-period schedule shows update prompt, no edit | Pass"
